Cautiously positive overall. The FOMC statement cites strengthening activity, solid job gains, and accommodative financial conditions despite elevated inflation and virus-related risks. The Beige Book around this period indicates growth continued but slowed to a modest pace amid Omicron-related disruptions—especially in leisure and hospitality and some retail—while supply bottlenecks and broad-based price pressures persisted. Labor markets remained very tight with strong wage growth and ongoing hiring difficulties, consistent with the FOMC’s “strong labor market” assessment. On the credit channel, District reports point to generally healthy or improving C&I loan demand and steady-to-strong consumer credit, which supports continued expansion, though residential real estate activity was constrained by low inventories and rising prices, and auto sales were hampered by shortages. Overall, Beige Book evidence tempers the near-term outlook relative to the initial read by highlighting Omicron and supply-side drags, but it does not overturn the positive trajectory given robust labor demand and supportive business credit conditions.
